chunks.section: Abstract
Abstract
chunks.text: 1 Introduction

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: Large language models (LLMs) are becoming a crucial building block in developing powerfulagents

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: that utilize LLMs for reasoning, tool usage, and adapting to new observations (Yao et al., 2022; Xi

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: et al., 2023; Wang et al., 2023b) in many real-world tasks. Given the expanding tasks that could

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: benefit from LLMs and the growing task complexity, an intuitive approach to scale up the power of

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: agents is to use multiple agents that cooperate. Prior work suggests that multiple agents can help

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: encourage divergent thinking (Liang et al., 2023), improve factuality and reasoning (Du et al., 2023),

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: and provide validation (Wu et al., 2023). In light of the intuition and early evidence of promise, it is

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: intriguing to ask the following question:how can we facilitate the development of LLM applications

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: that could span a broad spectrum of domains and complexities based on the multi-agent approach?

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: Our insight is to use multi-agent conversations to achieve it. There are at least three reasons con-

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: firming its general feasibility and utility thanks to recent advances in LLMs: First, because chat-

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: optimized LLMs (e.g., GPT-4) show the ability to incorporate feedback, LLM agents can cooperate

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: through conversations with each other or human(s), e.g., a dialog where agents provide and seek rea-

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: soning, observations, critiques, and validation. Second, because a single LLM can exhibit a broad

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: range of capabilities (especially when configured with the correct prompt and inference settings),

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: conversations between differently configured agents can help combine these broad LLM capabilities

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: in a modular and complementary manner. Third, LLMs have demonstrated ability to solve complex

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: tasks when the tasks are broken into simpler subtasks. Multi-agent conversations can enable this

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: partitioning and integration in an intuitive manner. How can we leverage the above insights and

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: support different applications with the common requirement of coordinating multiple agents, poten-

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: tially backed by LLMs, humans, or tools exhibiting different capacities? We desire a multi-agent

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: conversation framework with generic abstraction and effective implementation that has the flexibil-

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: ity to satisfy different application needs. Achieving this requires addressing two critical questions:

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: (1) How can we design individual agents that are capable, reusable, customizable, and effective in

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: multi-agent collaboration? (2) How can we develop a straightforward, unified interface that can

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: accommodate a wide range of agent conversation patterns? In practice, applications of varying

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: complexities may need distinct sets of agents with specific capabilities, and may require different

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: conversation patterns, such as single- or multi-turn dialogs, different human involvement modes, and

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: static vs. dynamic conversation. Moreover, developers may prefer the flexibility to program agent

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: interactions in natural language or code. Failing to adequately address these two questions would

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: limit the framework’s scope of applicability and generality.

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: While there is contemporaneous exploration of multi-agent approaches, 3 we present AutoGen, a

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: generalized multi-agent conversation framework (Figure 1), based on the following new concepts.

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: 1 Customizable and conversable agents. AutoGen uses a generic design of agents that can lever-

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: age LLMs, human inputs, tools, or a combination of them. The result is that developers can

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: easily and quickly create agents with different roles (e.g., agents to write code, execute code,

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: wire in human feedback, validate outputs, etc.) by selecting and configuring a subset of built-in

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: capabilities. The agent’s backend can also be readily extended to allow more custom behaviors.

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: To make these agents suitable for multi-agent conversation, every agent is made conversable –

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: they can receive, react, and respond to messages. When configured properly, an agent can hold

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: multiple turns of conversations with other agents autonomously or solicit human inputs at cer-

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: tain rounds, enabling human agency and automation. The conversable agent design leverages the

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: strong capability of the most advanced LLMs in taking feedback and making progress via chat

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: and also allows combining capabilities of LLMs in a modular fashion. (Section 2.1)

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: 2 Conversation programming. A fundamental insight of AutoGen is to simplify and unify com-

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: plex LLM application workflows as multi-agent conversations. So AutoGen adopts a program-

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: ming paradigm centered around these inter-agent conversations. We refer to this paradigm as

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: conversation programming, which streamlines the development of intricate applications via two

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: primary steps: (1) defining a set of conversable agents with specific capabilities and roles (as

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: described above); (2) programming the interaction behavior between agents via conversation-

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: centric computation and control. Both steps can be achieved via a fusion of natural and pro-

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: gramming languages to build applications with a wide range of conversation patterns and agent

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: behaviors. AutoGen provides ready-to-use implementations and also allows easy extension and

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: experimentation for both steps. (Section 2.2)

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: 3We refer to Appendix A for a detailed discussion.

chunks.section: Abstract
Abstract
chunks.text: AutoGen also provides a collection of multi-agent applications created using conversable agents

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: and conversation programming. These applications demonstrate how AutoGen can easily support

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: applications of various complexities and LLMs of various capabilities. Moreover, we perform both

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: evaluation on benchmarks and a pilot study of new applications. The results show thatAutoGen can

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: help achieve outstanding performance on many tasks, and enable innovative ways of using LLMs,

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: while reducing development effort. (Section 3 and Appendix D)

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: 2 The AutoGen Framework

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: To reduce the effort required for developers to create complex LLM applications across various do-

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: mains, a core design principle of AutoGen is to streamline and consolidate multi-agent workflows

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: using multi-agent conversations. This approach also aims to maximize the reusability of imple-

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: mented agents. This section introduces the two key concepts of AutoGen: conversable agents and

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: conversation programming.

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: 2.1 Conversable Agents

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: In AutoGen, a conversable agent is an entity with a specific role that can pass messages to send and

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: receive information to and from other conversable agents, e.g., to start or continue a conversation. It

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: maintains its internal context based on sent and received messages and can be configured to possess

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: a set of capabilities, e.g., enabled by LLMs, tools, or human input, etc. The agents can act according

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: to programmed behavior patterns described next.

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: Agent capabilities powered by LLMs, humans, and tools. Since an agent’s capabilities directly

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: influence how it processes and responds to messages,AutoGen allows flexibility to endow its agents

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: with various capabilities. AutoGen supports many common composable capabilities for agents,

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: including 1) LLMs. LLM-backed agents exploit many capabilities of advanced LLMs such as role

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: playing, implicit state inference and progress making conditioned on conversation history, providing

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: feedback, adapting from feedback, and coding. These capabilities can be combined in different ways

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: via novel prompting techniques 4 to increase an agent’s skill and autonomy. AutoGen also offers

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: enhanced LLM inference features such as result caching, error handling, message templating, etc.,

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: via an enhanced LLM inference layer. 2) Humans. Human involvement is desired or even essential

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: in many LLM applications. AutoGen lets a human participate in agent conversation via human-

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: backed agents, which could solicit human inputs at certain rounds of a conversation depending on

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: the agent configuration. The default user proxy agent allows configurable human involvement levels

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: and patterns, e.g., frequency and conditions for requesting human input including the option for

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: humans to skip providing input. 3) Tools. Tool-backed agents have the capability to execute tools

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: via code execution or function execution. For example, the default user proxy agent in AutoGen is

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: able to execute code suggested by LLMs, or make LLM-suggested function calls.

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: Agent customization and cooperation. Based on application-specific needs, each agent can be

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: configured to have a mix of basic back-end types to display complex behavior in multi-agent con-

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: versations. AutoGen allows easy creation of agents with specialized capabilities and roles by reusing

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: or extending the built-in agents. The yellow-shaded area of Figure 2 provides a sketch of the built-in

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: agents in AutoGen. The ConversableAgent class is the highest-level agent abstraction and, by

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: default, can use LLMs, humans, and tools. The AssistantAgent and UserProxyAgent are two

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: pre-configured ConversableAgent subclasses, each representing a common usage mode, i.e., act-

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: ing as an AI assistant (backed by LLMs) and acting as a human proxy to solicit human input or

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: execute code/function calls (backed by humans and/or tools).

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: In the example on the right-hand side of Figure 1, an LLM-backed assistant agent and a tool- and

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: human-backed user proxy agent are deployed together to tackle a task. Here, the assistant agent

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: generates a solution with the help of LLMs and passes the solution to the user proxy agent. Then,

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: the user proxy agent solicits human inputs or executes the assistant’s code and passes the results as

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: feedback back to the assistant.

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: 4Appendix C presents an example of such novel prompting techniques which empowers the default LLM-

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: backed assistant agent in AutoGen to converse with other agents in multi-step problem solving.

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: Unified Conversation Interfaces:•send•receive •generate_reply

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: Figure 2: Illustration of how to use AutoGen to program a multi-agent conversation. The top sub-

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: figure illustrates the built-in agents provided byAutoGen, which have unified conversation interfaces

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: and can be customized. The middle sub-figure shows an example of using AutoGen to develop

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: a two-agent system with a custom reply function. The bottom sub-figure illustrates the resulting

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: automated agent chat from the two-agent system during program execution.

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: By allowing custom agents that can converse with each other, conversable agents in AutoGen serve

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: as a useful building block. However, to develop applications where agents make meaningful progress

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: on tasks, developers also need to be able to specify and mold these multi-agent conversations.

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: 2.2 Conversation Programming

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: As a solution to the above problem, AutoGen utilizes conversation programming, a paradigm that

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: considers two concepts: the first is computation – the actions agents take to compute their response

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: in a multi-agent conversation. And the second is control flow – the sequence (or conditions) un-

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: der which these computations happen. As we will show in the applications section, the ability to

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: program these helps implement many flexible multi-agent conversation patterns. In AutoGen, these

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: computations are conversation-centric. An agent takes actions relevant to the conversations it is

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: involved in and its actions result in message passing for consequent conversations (unless a termina-

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: tion condition is satisfied). Similarly, control flow is conversation-driven – the participating agents’

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: decisions on which agents to send messages to and the procedure of computation are functions of the

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: inter-agent conversation. This paradigm helps one to reason intuitively about a complex workflow

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: as agent action taking and conversation message-passing between agents.

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: Figure 2 provides a simple illustration. The bottom sub-figure shows how individual agents perform

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: their role-specific, conversation-centric computations to generate responses (e.g., via LLM inference

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: calls and code execution). The task progresses through conversations displayed in the dialog box.

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: The middle sub-figure demonstrates a conversation-based control flow. When the assistant receives

chunks.section: Abstract

chunks.section: Abstract
Abstract
chunks.text: AutoGen features the following design patterns to facilitate conversation programming:

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: 1. Unified interfaces and auto-reply mechanisms for automated agent chat. Agents in

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: AutoGen have unified conversation interfaces for performing the corresponding conversation-

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: centric computation, including a send/receive function for sending/receiving messages and a

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: generate reply function for taking actions and generating a response based on the received

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: message. AutoGen also introduces and by default adopts an agent auto-reply mechanism to

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: realize conversation-driven control: Once an agent receives a message from another agent, it au-

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: tomatically invokes generate reply and sends the reply back to the sender unless a termination

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: condition is satisfied. AutoGen provides built-in reply functions based on LLM inference, code

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: or function execution, or human input. One can also register custom reply functions to customize

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: the behavior pattern of an agent, e.g., chatting with another agent before replying to the sender

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: agent. Under this mechanism, once the reply functions are registered, and the conversation is

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: initialized, the conversation flow is naturally induced, and thus the agent conversation proceeds

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: naturally without any extra control plane, i.e., a special module that controls the conversation

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: flow. For example, with the developer code in the blue-shaded area (marked “Developer Code”)

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: of Figure 2, one can readily trigger the conversation among the agents, and the conversation

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: would proceed automatically, as shown in the dialog box in the grey shaded area (marked “Pro-

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: gram Execution”) of Figure 2. The auto-reply mechanism provides a decentralized, modular, and

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: unified way to define the workflow.

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: 2. Control by fusion of programming and natural language. AutoGen allows the usage of

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: programming and natural language in various control flow management patterns: 1) Natural-

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: language control via LLMs. In AutoGen, one can control the conversation flow by prompting

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: the LLM-backed agents with natural language. For instance, the default system message of the

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: built-in AssistantAgent in AutoGen uses natural language to instruct the agent to fix errors

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: and generate code again if the previous result indicates there are errors. It also guides the agent

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: to confine the LLM output to certain structures, making it easier for other tool-backed agents to

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: consume. For example, instructing the agent to reply with “TERMINATE” when all tasks are

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: completed to terminate the program. More concrete examples of natural language controls can

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: be found in Appendix C. 2) Programming-language control. In AutoGen, Python code can be

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: used to specify the termination condition, human input mode, and tool execution logic, e.g., the

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: max number of auto replies. One can also register programmed auto-reply functions to control

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: the conversation flow with Python code, as shown in the code block identified as “Conversation-

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: Driven Control Flow” in Figure 2. 3) Control transition between natural and programming

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: language. AutoGen also supports flexible control transition between natural and programming

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: language. One can achieve transition from code to natural-language control by invoking an LLM

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: inference containing certain control logic in a customized reply function; or transition from nat-

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: ural language to code control via LLM-proposed function calls (Eleti et al., 2023).

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: In the conversation programming paradigm, one can realize multi-agent conversations of diverse

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: patterns. In addition to static conversation with predefined flow, AutoGen also supports dynamic

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: conversation flows with multiple agents. AutoGen provides two general ways to achieve this: 1)

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: Customized generate reply function: within the customized generate reply function, one

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: agent can hold the current conversation while invoking conversations with other agents depending

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: on the content of the current message and context. 2) Function calls: In this approach, LLM decides

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: whether or not to call a particular function depending on the conversation status. By messaging

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: additional agents in the called functions, the LLM can drive dynamic multi-agent conversation. In

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: addition, AutoGen supports more complex dynamic group chat via built-in GroupChatManager,

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: which can dynamically select the next speaker and then broadcast its response to other agents. We

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: elaborate on this feature and its application in Section 3. We provide implemented working systems

chunks.section: Abstract
chunks.text: to showcase all these different patterns, with some of them visualized in Figure 3.

chunks.text: SystemMessageYou are a helpful AI assistant. Solve tasks using your coding and language skills.In the following cases, suggest python code (in a python coding block) or shell script (in a shcoding block) for the user to execute.1. When you need to collect info, use the code to output the info you need, for example, browse or search the web, download/read a file, print the content of a webpage or a file, get the current date/time. After sufficient info is printed and the task is ready to be solved based on your language skill, you can solve the task by yourself.2. When you need to perform some task with code, use the code to perform the task and output theresult. Finish the task smartly.Solve the task step by step if you need to. If a plan is not provided, explain your plan first. Be clear which step uses code, and which step uses your language skill.When using code, you must indicate the script type in the code block. The user cannot provide any other feedback or perform any other action beyond executing the code you suggest. The user can’t modify your code. So do not suggest incomplete code which requires users to modify. Don’t use a code block if it’s not intended to be executed by the user.If you want the user to save the code in a file before executing it, put # filename: <filename> inside the code block as the first line. Don’t include multiple code blocks in one response. Do not ask users to copy and paste the result. Instead, use ’print’ function for the output when relevant. Check the execution result returned by the user.If the result indicates there is an error, fix the error and output the code again. Suggest the full code instead of partial code or code changes. If the error can’t be fixed or if the task is not solved even after the code is executed successfully, analyze the problem, revisit your assumption, collect additional info you need, and think of a different approach to try.When you find an answer, verify the answer carefully. Include verifiable evidence in your response if possible.Reply “TERMINATE” in the end when everything is done.

chunks.text: Scenario 3: Multi-User Problem Solving. Next-generation LLM applications may necessitate

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: the involvement of multiple real users for collectively solving a problem with the assistance of

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: LLMs. We showcase howAutoGen can be leveraged to effortlessly construct such a system. Specif-

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: ically, building upon scenario 2 mentioned above, we aim to devise a simple system involving two

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: human users: a student and an expert. In this setup, the student interacts with an LLM assistant to

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: address some problems, and the LLM automatically resorts to the expert when necessary.

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: The overall workflow is as follows: The student chats with the LLM-based assistant agent through

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: a student proxy agent to solve problems. When the assistant cannot solve the problem satisfactorily,

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: or the solution does not match the expectation of the student, it would automatically hold the con-

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: versation and call the pre-defined ask for expert function via the function call feature of GPT

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: in order to resort to the expert. Specifically, it would automatically produce the initial message for

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: the ask for expert function, which could be the statement of the problem or the request to verify

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: the solution to a problem, and the expert is supposed to respond to this message with the help of

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: the expert assistant. After the conversation between the expert and the expert’s assistant, the final

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: message would be sent back to the student assistant as the response to the initial message. Then, the

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: student assistant would resume the conversation with the student using the response from the expert

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: for a better solution. A detailed visualization is shown in Figure 6.

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: With AutoGen, constructing the student/expert proxy agent and the assistant agents is straight-

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: forward by reusing the built-in UserProxyAgent and AssistantAgent through appropriate

chunks.text: Figure 7: Overview of Retrieval-augmented Chat which involves two agents, including a Retrieval-

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: augmented User Proxy and a Retrieval-augmented Assistant. Given a set of documents, the

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: Retrieval-augmented User Proxy first automatically processes documents—splits, chunks, and stores

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: them in a vector database. Then for a given user input, it retrieves relevant chunks as context and

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: sends it to the Retrieval-augmented Assistant, which uses LLM to generate code or text to answer

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: questions. Agents converse until they find a satisfactory answer.

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: Detailed Workflow. The workflow of Retrieval-Augmented Chat is illustrated in Figure 7. To

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: use Retrieval-augmented Chat, one needs to initialize two agents including Retrieval-augmented

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: User Proxy and Retrieval-augmented Assistant. Initializing the Retrieval-Augmented User Proxy

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: necessitates specifying a path to the document collection. Subsequently, the Retrieval-Augmented

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: User Proxy can download the documents, segment them into chunks of a specific size, compute

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: embeddings, and store them in a vector database. Once a chat is initiated, the agents collaboratively

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: engage in code generation or question-answering adhering to the procedures outlined below:

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: 1. The Retrieval-Augmented User Proxy retrieves document chunks based on the embedding simi-

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: larity, and sends them along with the question to the Retrieval-Augmented Assistant.

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: 2. The Retrieval-Augmented Assistant employs an LLM to generate code or text as answers based

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: on the question and context provided. If the LLM is unable to produce a satisfactory response, it

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: is instructed to reply with “Update Context” to the Retrieval-Augmented User Proxy.

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: 3. If a response includes code blocks, the Retrieval-Augmented User Proxy executes the code and

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: sends the output as feedback. If there are no code blocks or instructions to update the context, it

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: terminates the conversation. Otherwise, it updates the context and forwards the question along

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: with the new context to the Retrieval-Augmented Assistant. Note that if human input solicitation

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: is enabled, individuals can proactively send any feedback, including Update Context”, to the

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: Retrieval-Augmented Assistant.

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: 4. If the Retrieval-Augmented Assistant receives “Update Context”, it requests the next most similar

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: chunks of documents as new context from the Retrieval-Augmented User Proxy. Otherwise, it

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: generates new code or text based on the feedback and chat history. If the LLM fails to generate

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: an answer, it replies with “Update Context” again. This process can be repeated several times.

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: The conversation terminates if no more documents are available for the context.

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: We utilize Retrieval-Augmented Chat in two scenarios. The first scenario aids in generating code

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: based on a given codebase. While LLMs possess strong coding abilities, they are unable to utilize

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: packages or APIs that are not included in their training data, e.g., private codebases, or have trouble

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: using trained ones that are frequently updated post-training. Hence, Retrieval-Augmented Code

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: Generation is considered to be highly valuable. The second scenario involves question-answering

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: on the Natural Questions dataset (Kwiatkowski et al., 2019), enabling us to obtain comparative

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: evaluation metrics for the performance of our system.

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: Scenario 1: Evaluation on Natural Questions QA dataset. In this case, we evaluate the

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: tions dataset (Kwiatkowski et al., 2019). We collected 5,332 non-redundant context documents and

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: 6,775 queries from HuggingFace. First, we create a document collection based on the entire context

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: corpus and store it in the vector database. Then, we utilize Retrieval-Augmented Chat to answer the

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: questions. An example (Figure 8) from the NQ dataset showcases the advantages of the interactive

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: In addition, we conduct an experiment using the same prompt as illustrated in (Adlakha et al., 2023)

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: to investigate the advantages of AutoGen W/O interactive retrieval. The F1 score and Recall for the

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: first 500 questions are 23.40% and 62.60%, respectively, aligning closely with the results reported

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: in Figure 4b. Consequently, we assert that AutoGen W/O interactive retrievaloutperforms DPR due

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: to differences in the retrievers employed. Specifically, we utilize a straightforward vector search

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: retriever with the all-MiniLM-L6-v2 model for embeddings.

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: Furthermore, we analyze the number of LLM calls in experiments involving both AutoGen and

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: AutoGen W/O interactive retrieval, revealing that approximately 19.4% of questions in the Natural

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: Questions dataset trigger an “Update Context” operation, resulting in additional LLM calls.

chunks.text: Scenario 2: Code Generation Leveraging Latest APIs from the Codebase.In this case, the ques-

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: tion is “How can I use FLAML to perform a classification task and use Spark for parallel training?

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: Train for 30 seconds and force cancel jobs if the time limit is reached. ”. FLAML (v1) (Wang et al.,

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: 2021) is an open-source Python library designed for efficient AutoML and tuning. It was open-

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: sourced in December 2020, and is included in the training data of GPT-4. However, the question

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: necessitates the use of Spark-related APIs, which were added in December 2022 and are not encom-

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: passed in the GPT-4 training data. Consequently, the original GPT-4 model is unable to generate the

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: correct code, due to its lack of knowledge regarding Spark-related APIs. Instead, it erroneously cre-

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: ates a non-existent parameter, spark, and sets it to True’. Nevertheless, with Retrieval-Augmented

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: Chat, we provide the latest reference documents as context. Then, GPT-4 generates the correct code

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: blocks by setting use spark and f orce cancel to True’.

chunks.text: Figure 9: We use AutoGen to solve tasks in the ALFWorld benchmark, which contains household

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: tasks described in natural language. We propose two designs: a two-agent design where the assistant

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: agent suggests the next step, and the Executor executes actions and provides feedback. The three-

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: agent design adds a grounding agent that supplies commonsense facts to the executor when needed.

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: ALFWorld (Shridhar et al., 2021) is a synthetic language-based interactive decision-making task.

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: It comprises textual environments that aim to simulate real-world household scenes. Given a high-

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: level goal (e.g., putting a hot apple in the fridge) and the description of the household environment,

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: the agent needs to explore and interact with the simulated household environment through a textual

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: interface. A typical task environment contains various types of locations and could require more

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: than 40 steps to finish, which highlights the need for agents to decompose the goal into subtasks and

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: tackle them one by one, while effectively exploring the environments.

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: Detailed Workflow.We first propose a straightforward two-agent system withAutoGen, illustrated

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: on the left-hand side of Figure 9, to tackle tasks from this benchmark. The system consists of

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: an assistant agent and an executor agent. The assistant agent generates plans and makes action

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: decisions to solve the tasks. The executor agent is tailored specifically for ALFWorld. It performs

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: actions proposed by the assistant and reports action execution results in the household environment

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: as feedback to the assistant. Due to the strict format requirements for the output format, we use the

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: BLEU metric to evaluate the similarity of the output to all valid action options. The option with the

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: highest similarity will be chosen as the action for this round.

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: One major challenge encompassed in ALFWorld is commonsense reasoning. The agent needs to

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: extract patterns from the few-shot examples provided and combine them with the agent’s general

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: knowledge of household environments to fully understand task rules. More often than not, the as-

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: sistant tends to neglect some basic knowledge of the household environment. Thanks to the easy-to-

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: implement multi-agent conversational feature of AutoGen, enhancing the assistant agent’s reason-

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: ing ability by adding a new grounding agent to provide commonsense facts for the decision-making

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: agent’s reference becomes straightforward. By scrutinizing the failed attempts and summarizing the

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: reasons for failure, we obtained a holistic understanding of the commonsense knowledge that the

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: assistant agent lacks. Then, we set a grounding agent to provide this general knowledge when the

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: task begins and whenever the assistant outputs the same action three times in a row. This ensures the

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: assistant takes this commonsense knowledge into consideration and prevents it from getting stuck in

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: outputting the same content or constantly apologizing.

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: We compare our system’s performance with ReAct, which treats ALFWorld as a text-completion

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: task. ReAct (Yao et al., 2022) is a few-shot prompting technique that interleaves reasoning and

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: acting, allowing for greater synergy between the two and significantly improving performance on

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: both language and decision-making tasks. We integrate ReAct into AutoGen by modifying the

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: prompts in a conversational manner. Following ReAct, we employ a two-shot setting. The few-

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: shot prompts are obtained from the corresponding repository. As shown in Table 3, the two-agent

chunks.text: Manual Evaluation Comparing ChatGPT + Code Interpreter and AutoGen-based OptiGuide.

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: ChatGPT + Code Interpreter is unable to execute code with private or customized dependencies (e.g.,

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: Gurobi), which means users need to have engineering expertise to manually handle multiple steps,

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: disrupting the workflow and increasing the chance for mistakes. If users lack access or expertise,

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: the burden falls on supporting engineers, increasing their on-call time.

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: We carried out a user study that juxtaposed OpenAI’s ChatGPT coupled with a Code Interpreter

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: against AutoGen-based OptiGuide. The study focused on a coffee supply chain scenario, and an

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: expert Python programmer with proficiency in Gurobi participated in the test. We evaluated both

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: systems based on 10 randomly selected questions, measuring time and accuracy. While both sys-

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: tems answered 8 questions correctly, the Code Interpreter was significantly slower than OptiGuide

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: because the former requires more manual intervention. On average, users needed to spend 4 minutes

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: and 35 seconds to solve problems with the Code Interpreter, with a standard deviation of approxi-

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: mately 2.5 minutes. In contrast, OptiGuide’s average problem-solving time was around 1.5 minutes,

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: most of which was spent waiting for responses from the GPT-4 model. This indicates a 3x saving

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: on the user’s time withAutoGen-based OptiGuide.

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: While using ChatGPT + Code Interpreter, users had to read through the code and instructions to

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: know where to paste the code snippets. Additionally, running the code involves downloading it and

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: executing it in a terminal, a process that was both time-consuming and prone to errors. The response

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: time from the Code Interpreter is also slower, as it generates lots of tokens to read the code, read the

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: variables line-by-line, perform chains of thought analysis, and then produce the final answer code.

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: To realize these scenarios, we constructed a player agent with LLM and human as back-end options.

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: When human input is enabled, before sending the input to the board agent, it first prompts the human

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: player to input the message that contains the move along with anything else the player wants to say

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: (such as a witty comment). If human input is skipped or disabled, LLM is used to generate the

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: message. The board agent is implemented with a custom reply function, which employs an LLM

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: to parse the natural language input into a legal move in a structured format (e.g., UCI), and then

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: pushes the move to the board. If the move is not legitimate, the board agent will reply with an error.

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: Subsequently, the player agent needs to resend a message to the board agent until a legal move is

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: made. Once the move is successfully pushed, the player agent sends the message to the opponent.

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: As shown in Figure 15, the conversation between AI players can be natural and entertaining. When

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: the player agent uses LLM to generate a message, it utilizes the board state and the error message

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: from the board agent. This helps reduce the chance of hallucinating an invalid move. The chat

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: between one player agent and the board agent is invisible to the other player agent, which helps

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: keep the messages used in chat completion well-managed.

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: There are two notable benefits of using AutoGen to implement Conversational Chess. Firstly, the

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: agent design in AutoGen facilitates the natural creation of objects and their interactions needed in

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: our chess game. This makes development easy and intuitive. For example, the isolation of chat

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: messages simplifies the process of making a proper LLM chat completion inference call. Secondly,

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: AutoGen greatly simplifies the implementation of agent behaviors using composition. Specifically,

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: we utilized the register reply method supported by AutoGen agents to instantiate player agents

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: and a board agent with custom reply functions. Concentrating the extension work needed at a single

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: point (the reply function) simplifies the reasoning processes, and development and maintenance

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: effort.

chunks.text: Figure 17: We use AutoGen to build MiniWobChat, which solves tasks in the MiniWob++ bench-

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: mark. MiniWobChat consists of two agents: an assistant agent and an executor agent. The assistant

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: agent suggests actions to manipulate the browser while the executor executes the suggested actions

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: and returns rewards/feedback. The assistant agent records the feedback and continues until the feed-

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: back indicates task success or failure.

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: In practice, many applications require the presence of agents capable of interacting with environ-

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: ments and making decisions in an online context, such as in game playing (Mnih et al., 2013; Vinyals

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: et al., 2017), web interactions (Liu et al., 2018; Shi et al., 2017), and robot manipulations (Shen

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: et al., 2021). With the multi-agent conversational framework in AutoGen, it becomes easy to de-

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: compose the automatic agent-environment interactions and the development of a decision-making

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: agent by constructing an executor agent responsible for handling the interaction with the environ-

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: ment, thereby delegating the decision-making part to other agents. Such a decomposition allows

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: developers to reuse the decision-making agent for new tasks with minimal effort rather than build-

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: ing a specialized decision-making agent for every new environment.

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: Workflow. We demonstrate how to use AutoGen to build a working system for handling such

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: scenarios with the MiniWoB++ benchmark (Shi et al., 2017). MiniWoB++ comprises browser in-

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: teraction tasks that involve utilizing mouse and keyboard actions to interact with browsers. The

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: ultimate objective of each task is to complete the tasks described concisely in natural language, such

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: as “expand the web section below and click the submit button.” Solving these tasks typically requires

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: a sequence of web manipulation actions rather than a single action, and making action decisions at

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: each time step requires access to the web status (in the form of HTML code) online. For the example

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: above, clicking the submit button requires checking the web status after expanding the web section.

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: We designed a straightforward two-agent system named MiniWobChat usingAutoGen, as shown in

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: Figure 17. The assistant agent is an instance of the built-in AssistantAgent and is responsible for

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: making action decisions for the given task. The second agent, the executor agent, is a customized

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: UserProxyAgent, which is responsible for interacting with the benchmark by executing the actions

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: suggested by the AssistantAgent and returning feedback.

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: To assess the performance of the developed working system, we compare it with RCI (Kim et al.,

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: 2023), a recent solution for the MiniWoB++ benchmark that employs a set of self-critiquing prompts

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: and has achieved state-of-the-art performance. In our evaluation, we use all available tasks in the

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: official RCI code, with varying degrees of difficulty, to conduct a comprehensive analysis against

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: MiniWobChat. Figure 18 illustrates that MiniWobChat achieves competitive performance in this

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: evaluation8. Specifically, among the 49 available tasks, MiniWobChat achieves a success rate of

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: 52.8%, which is only 3.6% lower than RCI, a method specifically designed for the MiniWob++

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: benchmark. It is worth noting that in most tasks, the difference between the two methods is mirrored

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: as shown in Figure 18. If we consider 0.1 as a success rate tolerance for each task, i.e., two methods

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: that differ within 0.1 are considered to have the same performance, both methods outperform the

chunks.text: Additionally, we also explored the feasibility of using Auto-GPT for handling the same tasks. Auto-

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: GPT faces challenges in handling tasks that involve complex rules due to its limited extensibility.

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: It provides an interface for setting task goals using natural language. However, when dealing with

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: the MiniWob++ benchmark, accurately instructing Auto-GPT to follow the instructions for using

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: Takeaways: For this application, AutoGen stood out as a more user-friendly option, offering mod-

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: ularity and programmability: It streamlined the process with autonomous conversations between the

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: assistant and executor, and provided readily available solutions for agent-environment interactions.

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: The built-in AssistantAgent was directly reusable and exhibited strong performance without cus-

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: tomization. Moreover, the decoupling of the execution and assistant agent ensures that modifications

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: to one component do not adversely impact the other. This convenience simplifies maintenance and

chunks.section: results, including the correct answer, but GPT-4 always
chunks.text: future updates.
